To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the control and coordination costs associated with outsourcing complex global services are influenced by task- and location specific complexity.”

the degree of service complexity, geographic distance between customer and provider locations, and the degree of customization and cultural distance are significantly associated with the control and coordination cost of global outsourcing relationships.

(1) the scale of the outsourced service, geographic distance between provider and client locations, and the degree of geographic dispersion are all associated with higher levels and costs of control; (2) the breadth of the service and geographic dispersion are associated with increased control but not coordination costs; (3) service customization is negatively related to control costs, whereas both control- and coordination costs are positively related to the degree of cultural distance between provider- and customer organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of task- & location-specific complexity on outsourcing relationships.
the costs associated with managing global outsourcing relationships and the factors that influence those costs.
the costs of outsourcing and the influence of the task and location characteristics of the outsourced service on these costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more complex the task and the more dispersed the location, the higher the costs associated with managing outsourcing relationships.
the more complex the task or location, the more control and coordination costs will be incurred.
the higher the complexity of the service task, the greater the degree of control costs, but that the greater the complexity of the location-specific factors, the lower the degree of control cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
outsourcing organizations need to consider the complexity of their tasks and their location-specific factors when deciding how much control and coordination costs to incur.
the complexity of the task and location of the service provider have a significant impact on the control and coordinating costs associated with managing an outsourcing relationship.
the degree of complexity in outsourcing relationships influences the level of costs incurred by organizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
managers need to be cognizant of the potential for increased control and coordination costs when engaging in complex, global outsourcing relationships.
outsourcing organizations need to carefully consider the task and location-specific complexity characteristics of the services they are considering outsourcing.
the degree of complexity of outsourced services is a key driver of control and coordination cost.
